title: Girls volleyball: King Kekaulike sweeps two, Seabury Hall stays perfect
excerpt: King Kekaulike swept Lahainaluna and Kamehameha Maui, Baldwin and Maui High each won a five-set match, and Seabury Hall improved to 10–0 in MIL Division II.
body:
King Kekaulike swept Lahainaluna and Kamehameha Maui, Baldwin and Maui High each won a five-set match, and Seabury Hall improved to 10–0 in MIL Division II.

King Kekaulike had a big stretch in MIL Division I girls volleyball. It beat Lahainaluna 3–0 (25–20, 25–20, 25–21) at home on Tuesday, Oct. 6, then swept Kamehameha Maui 3–0 (25–22, 25–17, 27–25) on Tuesday, Oct. 13.

Also on Oct. 6, Kamehameha Maui won 3–1 at Baldwin (27–25, 22–25, 26–24, 25–15). On Thursday, Oct. 8, Maui High dropped the first two sets to Lahainaluna, then came back to win 3–2 (17–25, 22–25, 25–15, 25–16, 15–10). Maui High went five again on Oct. 13, and this time Baldwin won it at home, 3–2 (22–25, 25–15, 11–25, 25–16, 15–8).

In Division II, Seabury Hall swept Maui Prep 3–0 (25–16, 25–16, 25–19) at home on Wednesday, Oct. 14. That’s 10 straight wins and a 10–0 league record for the Spartans, who host Kūlanihākoʻi on Friday, Oct. 16, at 6 p.m.

title: Weekend roundup: King Kekaulike rolls, Lahainaluna edges Maui; Hāna sweeps volleyball
excerpt: King Kekaulike beat Kūlanihākoʻi 53–0, Lahainaluna held off Maui High 15–12, Hāna won twice in girls volleyball, and Seabury Hall beat Lānaʻi 3–1.
body:
King Kekaulike beat Kūlanihākoʻi 53–0, Lahainaluna held off Maui High 15–12, Hāna won twice in girls volleyball, and Seabury Hall beat Lānaʻi 3–1.

King Kekaulike shut out Kūlanihākoʻi 53–0 on Friday, Oct. 9, its fourth straight home win. On Saturday, Oct. 10, Lahainaluna held off Maui High 15–12 at home in its first conference game.

In girls volleyball on Friday, Oct. 9, Hāna beat Kīhei Charter 3–0 and Kūlanihākoʻi beat Haleakalā Waldorf 3–0. On Saturday, Oct. 10, Seabury Hall beat Lānaʻi 3–1, and Hāna won again at Kīhei Charter, 3–0 (25–15, 25–8, 25–10).

body:
Kamehameha Maui shut out Kūlanihākoʻi 59–0, Seabury Hall beat Maui Prep 3–0, and Molokaʻi and Hāna each won a girls volleyball match.

title: Fall-break junior golf clinic set for October 7 at The Dunes
excerpt: HSJGA lists a junior skills clinic at The Dunes at Maui Lani on Wednesday, Oct. 7, from 4 to 5:30 p.m.
body:
HSJGA lists a junior skills clinic at The Dunes at Maui Lani on Wednesday, Oct. 7, from 4 to 5:30 p.m.

The Hawaiʻi State Junior Golf Association announced fall-break instruction for junior golfers at The Dunes at Maui Lani on Oct. 7, from 4 to 5:30 p.m.

The clinic covers swing technique and golf fundamentals with PGA and LPGA instructors. The published fee is $49, including a hat and refreshments. Check the organizer’s registration link for available places.

title: Fall youth flag football enters late registration ahead of October 17 kickoff
excerpt: Maui Sports Leagues lists late registration through Oct. 24 at $140, with the fall season scheduled to begin Oct. 17.
body:
Maui Sports Leagues lists late registration through Oct. 24 at $140, with the fall season scheduled to begin Oct. 17.

Regular pricing ended Sept. 30. Maui Sports Leagues’ published late-registration window runs Oct. 1–24 at $140.

The season is scheduled Oct. 17–Dec. 12, with coed 4U–14U and girls 8U–16U divisions. Families must obtain a team coach’s approval before registering; the league states that payments are nonrefundable. Contact the league about openings and team placement.

title: Free Surf-N-Turf youth program heads into final September session
excerpt: Mana O Maui’s free Surf-N-Turf afterschool program is scheduled to hold the final session of its September series on Wednesday, Sept. 30.
body:
Mana O Maui’s free Surf-N-Turf afterschool program is scheduled to hold the final session of its September series on Wednesday, Sept. 30.

The program serves Maui youth ages 11 to 17 and combines surfing or hiking depending on conditions. The September series was scheduled for four Wednesdays, with transportation offered from Central Maui pickup points.

The program is designed to get young people outdoors after school while providing structured recreation and access to Maui’s natural environment.

title: Menehune Basketball League continues through December
excerpt: The County of Maui’s 2026 Menehune Basketball League is underway, giving sixth-, seventh- and eighth-grade players a fall basketball season at County gyms around Maui.
body:
The County of Maui’s 2026 Menehune Basketball League is underway, giving sixth-, seventh- and eighth-grade players a fall basketball season at County gyms around Maui.

The Department of Parks and Recreation scheduled the league from Sept. 1 through Dec. 10. Registration was free, and the County said registered players would be placed on teams.

The program is one of the County’s recurring youth-sports offerings and provides a recreational basketball option for Maui middle-school-age players.

title: Fall youth flag football registration enters final days of regular pricing
excerpt: Maui Sports Leagues’ Phase 1 Fall 2026 youth flag football registration remains open, with regular registration scheduled through Sept. 30.
body:

The fall league lists coed divisions from 4U through 14U and girls divisions from 8U through 16U. The season is scheduled for Oct. 17 through Dec. 12, with league-wide breaks on Halloween and Thanksgiving weekend.

Regular registration is listed at $120. Late registration is scheduled from Oct. 1 through Oct. 24 at $140, subject to league availability and policies.

title: Maui golfers Austin and Lee win divisions at Maui Junior Championship
excerpt: Two Maui junior golfers finished atop their divisions at the Maui Junior Championship at Kāʻanapali Royal Golf Course. Artie Austin of Wailuku won the 9-Hole Flight, while Lakota Lee of Kīhei won the Boys 15–18 division.
body:
Two Maui junior golfers finished atop their divisions at the Maui Junior Championship at Kāʻanapali Royal Golf Course. Artie Austin of Wailuku won the 9-Hole Flight, while Lakota Lee of Kīhei won the Boys 15–18 division.

The Hawaiʻi State Junior Golf Association | First Tee – Hawaiʻi event was played Aug. 29–30 and drew 50 junior golfers from around the state. The 36-hole championship also awarded points toward the association’s Player of the Year standings and December Tour Championship.

For Maui families, the results put two local players at the top of their respective divisions in a statewide junior field on a Maui course.
